verdicts.summary: The deferred settle is never re-checked against what the user did after the agent asked. A pin or unsettle the user makes during the rest of the turn is silently undone when the run completes. The agent also has no way to cancel the pending settle.
verdicts.scenario: 1. The agent calls t3_thread_organize action=settle on its own thread mid-turn. settleThread forks settleAfterRun and returns { settlesWhenTurnEnds: true } (ThreadManagementService.ts:771-777). 2. While the turn is still running, the user pins the thread, or unsettles it to keep it active. Both are allowed during an active run, since the only guard is the archived check at Orchestrator.ts:2494-2511, and they set pinnedAt or settledOverride='active' (Orchestrator.ts:2787-2850). 3. The run completes. settleAfterRun sees status 'completed' and dispatches thread.settle with no check for anything that changed since the agent's request (ThreadManagementService.ts:759-764). 4. The settle reducer sets settledOverride='settled' and clears pinnedAt, pinOrderKey and activeOrderKey (Orchestrator.ts:2769-2785). The same happens if the agent itself calls unsettle later in the turn to take the request back: unsettle runs immediately, then the deferred settle runs anyway.
verdicts.consequence: A thread the user pinned or kept active during the turn ends up settled and unpinned with no notice to the user. The provider session also stops, because thread.settle needs provider state (Orchestrator.ts:2641). Before this change a settle while the run was active was refused, so it could never override a later user action.

verdicts.summary: I tried a run that stays in 'waiting' (not terminal, ProjectionStore.ts:1534-1541) for more than 24h, a thread deleted mid-wait, and a stream error. In every case the result is a silent no-settle or a failure that is only logged, and a fiber plus two streams held for the whole wait. Finding 0 already reports the logged-only failures and the 24h fibers. The layer scope is long-lived (Layer.effect, ThreadManagementService.ts:915-916), so the fork itself is sound.
